stem: A client with chemotherapy-induced oral mucositis has painful oral ulcers but can still tolerate gentle toothbrushing. Which oral-care plan is most appropriate?

options.A: Use a soft-bristle toothbrush with gentle cleaning, frequent bland rinses to keep the mouth moist and clear of debris, and prescribed pain-control measures as needed.
options.B: Stop mechanical tooth cleaning and use foam swabs as the routine substitute because foam swabs remove dental plaque more effectively than a soft toothbrush.
options.C: Use an alcohol-based mouthwash frequently because the burning sensation confirms that the ulcers are being disinfected effectively.
options.D: Avoid all oral care until the ulcers heal because cleaning the mouth delays recovery from mucositis.

rationale: A is correct. NCI guidance for mucositis supports continued gentle oral hygiene with a soft-bristle toothbrush, frequent mild or bland rinses, moisture maintenance, and pain-relief measures. The NCI health-professional PDQ states that foam-swab brushes do not effectively clean teeth and should not routinely replace a soft nylon-bristled toothbrush. B is therefore incorrect when gentle toothbrushing is tolerated. C is incorrect because NCI advises avoiding alcohol-containing mouthwashes in clients with oral complications. D is incorrect because ongoing gentle oral cleaning is part of mucositis care rather than something to stop until ulcers heal.
educational_objective: Provide oral care for established mucositis by maintaining gentle mechanical cleaning with a soft toothbrush when tolerated, using bland rinses and pain control, and avoiding routine foam-swab substitution or alcohol-containing mouthwash.
source_organization: National Cancer Institute (NCI), National Institutes of Health
source_document_title: Oral Complications of Cancer Therapies (PDQ®) — Patient Version; Oral Complications of Cancer Therapies (PDQ®) — Health Professional Version; Mouth and Throat Problems: Cancer Treatment Side Effects
source_locator: Patient PDQ — 'Regular Oral Care' and 'Care of mucositis during chemotherapy and radiation therapy includes cleaning the mouth and relieving pain'; Health Professional PDQ — oral hygiene section stating soft toothbrush use, foam-swab limitations, frequent bland saline/sodium-bicarbonate rinses, and recommendation against alcohol-based/astringent commercial mouthwashes for oral complications; Mouth and Throat Problems — 'Ways to prevent mouth and dental problems' and 'Ways to manage mouth problems'.
source_claim_supported: Gentle soft-bristle brushing, bland rinses and pain management are appropriate for mucositis; foam swabs do not routinely substitute for effective tooth cleaning; alcohol-containing mouthwash should be avoided in oral complications.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort — assistance with hygiene, comfort measures, and nonpharmacologic/supportive interventions that promote comfort and maintain basic care needs.
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source item to correct the implication that foam swabs are equivalent to a soft toothbrush and to specify that gentle brushing is tolerated, eliminating ambiguity while anchoring every intervention to current NCI guidance.
audit_findings: Fresh NCI review directly supports soft-bristle brushing, bland rinses, and pain relief for established mucositis.
NCI professional guidance explicitly states that foam swabs do not effectively clean teeth and should not routinely replace a soft toothbrush.
The stem states that gentle brushing is tolerated, preventing a conditional second answer involving limited foam-swab use.
Alcohol-based mouthwash and complete cessation of oral care are directly inconsistent with NCI guidance.
Independent adversarial review found no ambiguity, second answer, cueing, unsupported intervention, source-locator defect, or unresolved conflict.
